correctness.rationale: Every binary incidence-kernel word is constant on each of the r internally disjoint paths, and the two endpoint parity equations reduce to a single even-parity condition. Classifying block majority deviations yields an exact minimum-distance identity; parity pairs words with opposite baseline parity and equal deviation vector, giving both displayed polynomials. Strict inequalities valid for at least four paths establish the covering radii and the complete deep-hole types; tied and untied cases give their precise nearest-codeword counts. Replayed standalone brute enumeration of graph kernels, each ambient word and each nearest-codeword multiplicity for five parameter pairs produced VERIFY_OK. Finite verification is not substituted for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The full text of arXiv:2610.04617v1 Section 3.2 establishes the graph-derived code and minimum distance but not its complete ambient distance spectrum. General covering-radius results and parity-check product-code weight enumerators are closer neighbors but are mathematically different invariants; the former can imply only a radius, and the latter count codewords rather than all ambient words by nearest distance. Semantic searches of published published-finding corpus findings plus deduplication of prior internal claim identifiers revealed no comparable all-parameter ambient spectrum. This is a qualified originality assessment, not a uniqueness assertion; plausible older sources were available only as abstracts.
residual_risks: The full text of Solé--Zaslavsky (1993) was not accessed; some or all exact theta-family covering results could already be there.
The full arXiv:2608.26457 text was not accessed, so the path-length-two product-code special case might have an implicit equivalent computation.
Repeated parity-check majority decoding is a classical idea; another treatment could state the same ambient shell generating polynomial under a Voronoi, T-join, or coset-leader name.
published-finding corpus retrieval and search absence cannot exclude all published or unpublished results.

value.rationale: The all-parameter ambient distance enumerator is a complete, natural invariant of the recent family of graph cycle codes, quantifying nearest-codeword distance for every received word rather than merely codeword weights. It yields exact decoding tail probabilities at every radius and distinguishes worst-case tie multiplicities for odd/even path lengths, with explicit formulas replacing full ambient enumeration. These quantities are motivated by covering reliability and decoding ambiguity and are not direct consequences of the source parameters; the result treats an infinite family and all weight shells together.
